title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The handwritten notes are on the reverse of a typed page; the mirror-image typescript shows through. The neighbouring typed pages are chapter IX, §13 (analytic exponential, analytic Raynaud extension A^natural = E/R^f), which looks like a Mazur–Messing-type manuscript. They are unrelated to the handwritten content. The handwriting works in the topos Δ^ of simplicial sets (or simplicial sheaves Δ^(S_s) over a site S_s). The aim is to build the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex simplicially.

(1) A claim is completing the previous page, marked in the margin 'pour tel quel, à arranger!'. It says: 'flasque + flat ⇒ homotopic to 0 (by direct computation), hence universally flasque, and the Γ^i(L), i>0, universally flasque.' In modern terms: a contractible simplicial module L stays contractible after base change. By Dold–Puppe, any functor F with F(0)=0, for example the divided powers Γ^i (i>0), sends contractible simplicial modules to contractible ones.

(2) For each n there is a point i_n: P → Δ^ given by the fibre functor K ↦ K_n = K(Δ_n). For i_0 the direct image is computed by adjunction:
i_{0*}(M)([n]) = Hom(Δ_n, i_{0*}M) = Hom(i_0^*Δ_n, M) = M^{Hom(Δ_0,Δ_n)} = M^{[n]}.
So i_{0*}M is the 0-coskeleton n ↦ M^{n+1}, the right adjoint of evaluation in degree 0. For a k-module M it equals L_*⊗_Z M = L_{*k}⊗_k M, where L_*(I) = Z^I is the simplicial abelian group of functions on the vertices.

(3) Corollary (adjunction). For any module A_* over the constant simplicial ring k_*:
Hom_{k_*}(A_*, L_{*k}⊗M) = Hom_k(A_0, M).
Taking M = A_0 gives the canonical 'vertex' map A_* → L_*⊗A_0 = i_{0*}i_0^*A_*, sending A_n to A_0^{n+1}.
Note that L_*⊗M is contractible, since π_0 = M/(d_0−d_1) = 0 and it is the coskeleton of a nonempty object. This is the link back to (1).

(4) The page starts applying this to an augmentation u: k_* → A_* = A^{1,0}_* coming from an object A^•_* of Alg(S_s, k_*), a simplicial (graded/dg) algebra. Presumably the next step is to take the kernel of the vertex map, or of the augmentation, and its PD-filtration, to produce the PD de Rham complex. This is a simplicial / Alexander–Spanier style description of differential forms via the diagonal.
errors: The implication 'flasque + plat ⇒ homotope à 0' cannot hold for the ordinary topos-theoretic notion of flasque in Δ^. The terminal object Δ_0 has only trivial subobjects, so every object would be flasque, yet the constant simplicial module Z is flat and not contractible. Grothendieck's own marginal note 'pour tel quel, à arranger!' flags that the statement needs fixing. Read correctly, the property is something like 'coskeletal / of the form i_{0*}(flat)', which does imply contractible.
Minor point: the isomorphism i_{0*}M ≅ L_*⊗M uses that the I involved are finite (M^I = Z^I⊗M). This holds in Δ.

ideas.what: Direct image along the degree-0 point of Δ^ is the 0-coskeleton n ↦ M^{n+1}, i.e. L_*⊗M with L_*(I) = Z^I.
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard simplicial homotopy theory (Kan, Dold, Verdier's coskeleta in SGA4)
ideas.where_published: coskeleton formalism in SGA 4 Exp. V bis (Saint-Donat/Deligne), in the hypercovering context

ideas.what: Coskeletal modules L_*⊗M are contractible, and divided powers Γ^i (i>0) of contractible simplicial modules are contractible ('universally flasque').
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Puppe: non-additive functors preserve simplicial homotopy

ideas.what: Canonical vertex map A_* → i_{0*}i_0^*A_* = A_0^{[*]} for a simplicial algebra, to be combined with an augmentation of a simplicial dg-algebra, aiming at a simplicial construction of the PD de Rham complex.
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander / combinatorial (diagonal) description of the PD de Rham complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 'Crystals and de Rham cohomology' (1968), Berthelot, Illusie; Breen–Messing 'Combinatorial differential forms' (2001); Bhatt's derived de Rham (2012)
ideas.where_published: The 1976 IHÉS lecture on the PD de Rham complex appears unpublished

missed.claim: This is the start of a simplicial-topos construction of the divided-power de Rham complex. It uses the 0-coskeleton point i_{0*} and the homotopy-triviality of Γ^i of coskeletal modules, applied to augmented simplicial dg-algebras. The thread breaks off at 'Appliquons cela au cas d'une augmentation'.
missed.quote: Appliquons cela au cas d'une augmentation k_* → A_* = A^{1,0}_* provenant d'une A^•_* ∈ Ob Alg(S_s, k_*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early instance of the idea later developed as combinatorial/simplicial PD differential forms (Breen–Messing) and derived de Rham cohomology via simplicial resolutions (Illusie, Bhatt). It may be of historical interest for the unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture. The page itself contains only routine lemmas.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is a routine adjunction computation: the direct image along the 0-th point is the 0-coskeleton. There is also a homotopy-triviality claim that Grothendieck himself flags as needing repair. The only interest is as a trace of his unpublished simplicial approach to the PD de Rham complex, a line later explored by others.
transcription_corrections: The handwritten text is on the verso of a typed page; the faint mirror typescript is unrelated to the handwritten content.
'le topos [?] Δ^' : the superscript above 'topos' looks like '(Ss)', i.e. 'le topos Δ^(S_s)', consistent with i_n: P → Δ^(S_s) below.
The left-margin note reads roughly 'faux tel quel, à arranger!' or 'pour tel quel, à arranger!'; either way it flags the statement 'flasque + plat ⇒ homotope à 0' as needing correction.
'Δ^_cs ≃ Hom(Δ°, Ab)' : the subscript is unclear; from context it should denote abelian objects of Δ^ (simplicial abelian groups).
In the line 'A_* → L_*⊗_Z A_0 ≅ L_{*k}⊗_k A_0 (= i_{0*}i_0^*A_*)', 'Hom' is struck out before A_*; the final parenthesis is correctly i_{0*}i_0^* A_*.

The penultimate line plausibly reads 'Appliquons cela au cas d'une augmentation' (first '[?]'). The final 'A^•_* ∈ Ob Alg(S_s, k_*)' may carry a bar or decoration on 'Alg' (e.g. a graded or differential algebra category).
